title: Interfaces

notes: Sensor is the contract: read() and unit().
report() is a default method built from the other two.
SoilMoisture overrides the default with its own wording.
The loop only knows about Sensor, not the real classes.
An anonymous class makes a fake sensor for testing in two lines.

exercises.title: Field shapes
exercises.prompt: Plots of land come in shapes. interface Shape has area(), name() and a default describe() (done). Circle is done. Finish Rect(double w, double h) with name "rect" and Triangle(double base, double height) with name "triangle" (area = base × height / 2). In class Shapes write static double totalArea(List<Shape> shapes) rounded to 2 decimals, and static String largest(List<Shape> shapes) giving the name of the biggest shape, or "none" for an empty list.

tests.call: Shapes.largest(java.util.List.of(new Rect(1, 1), new Circle(1), new Triangle(2, 2)))

hints: Give Rect and Triangle private final fields and set them in the constructors.
totalArea: loop with for (Shape s : shapes) and add s.area().
largest: keep the best Shape so far; if the list is empty return "none".

exercises.title: Things that take damage
exercises.prompt: interface Damageable has takeDamage(int amount) and getHealth(). Make its default method isDestroyed() return true when health is 0 or less. Write three classes: Player (starts at 100 health; armour halves damage using integer division, amount / 2), Crate (30 health, takes full damage), Wall (200 health, ignores any hit below 10, otherwise full damage). Health never goes below 0. In Combat write static int hitAll(List<Damageable> things, int amount): hit every thing once and return how many are destroyed afterwards.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Player p = new Player(); p.takeDamage(30); return p.getHealth() + ""; }).get()
tests.name: armour halves damage

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Crate c = new Crate(); c.takeDamage(50); return c.getHealth() + " " + c.isDestroyed(); }).get()
tests.name: crate breaks

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Wall w = new Wall(); w.takeDamage(5); String a = w.getHealth() + ""; w.takeDamage(50); return a + " " + w.getHealth(); }).get()
tests.name: wall ignores small hits

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { java.util.List<Damageable> xs = java.util.List.of(new Player(), new Crate(), new Wall()); return Combat.hitAll(xs, 40) + ""; }).get()
tests.name: hitAll

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Player p = new Player(); p.takeDamage(300); return p.getHealth() + " " + p.isDestroyed(); }).get()
tests.name: health never negative

hints: Each class keeps private int health = 100 (or 30, 200).
health = Math.max(0, health - amount / 2); keeps it at 0 or more.

exercises.title: Clinic reminders
exercises.prompt: interface Notifier { void send(String to, String message); } is given. Write class MemoryNotifier implements Notifier: it stores each message as "to: message" in a list returned by getSent(). Write class Reminder with constructor Reminder(Notifier notifier) and int remindLate(Map<String, Integer> daysLate): for every patient whose days late is above 0 (in the map's order), send them "visit 3 days late" ("visit 1 day late" for exactly 1) and return how many were sent. Reminder must only use the Notifier interface.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { MemoryNotifier mem = new MemoryNotifier(); java.util.Map<String, Integer> m = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>(); m.put("Amina", 3); m.put("Juma", 0); m.put("Otieno", 1); int n = new Reminder(mem).remindLate(m); return n + " " + mem.getSent(); }).get()
tests.expect: 2 [Amina: visit 3 days late, Otieno: visit 1 day late]
tests.name: reminders sent

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { int[] count = {0}; java.util.Map<String, Integer> m = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>(); m.put("Wanjiru", 5); m.put("Akinyi", 2); new Reminder((to, msg) -> count[0]++).remindLate(m); return count[0] + ""; }).get()
tests.name: works with any Notifier (a lambda)

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { MemoryNotifier mem = new MemoryNotifier(); mem.send("Ali", "hello"); return mem.getSent().toString(); }).get()
tests.name: MemoryNotifier

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { MemoryNotifier mem = new MemoryNotifier(); int n = new Reminder(mem).remindLate(new java.util.HashMap<>()); return n + " " + mem.getSent().size(); }).get()
tests.name: no patients

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { MemoryNotifier mem = new MemoryNotifier(); java.util.Map<String, Integer> m = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>(); m.put("Juma", -2); return new Reminder(mem).remindLate(m) + ""; }).get()
tests.name: negative days are not late

hints: Reminder keeps the notifier in a private final Notifier field.
Loop with for (var e : daysLate.entrySet()) and skip values <= 0.
String msg = "visit " + d + (d == 1 ? " day late" : " days late"); notifier.send(e.getKey(), msg);

quiz.q: What does an interface give you?
choices: A contract of methods; any class can promise to have them
A way to make objects without new
quiz.why: It lists what implementers must provide.

choices: Compile error: you can't instantiate an interface
Works if it has default methods
quiz.why: Make objects of implementing classes instead.

quiz.q: You add a new Barrel class that implements Damageable. What must change in hitAll(List<Damageable>)?
quiz.why: That's the point of programming to the interface.

quiz.q: A default method in an interface…
choices: has a body that implementers get for free (and may override)
can read the class's private fields
quiz.why: Defaults are built from the interface's other methods.

quiz.q: Why use a MemoryNotifier in tests instead of real SMS?
choices: Tests can check what was sent without sending anything real
quiz.why: Swap the part behind the interface for a fake you can inspect.

cards.q: Keyword to sign an interface's contract?
How many interfaces can a class implement?
cards.a: As many as it needs: implements A, B, C
Variables and parameters use the interface type, so any implementation fits.
An interface with one abstract method: you can pass a lambda for it.

explain: Explain an interface as a contract, using an example from a game or a farm tool you'd like to build. What does the code that USES the interface gain?
